claims.claim: **Preschool asthma = age 1–5 with recurrent cough, wheeze or difficulty breathing/activity limitation, each of which responds to SABA.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most preschool children have infrequent mild viral wheeze** (over 6 weeks between episodes) **and do not need a preventer.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Wheeze under 1 year is most likely bronchiolitis.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not sub-type preschool wheeze** — 'viral-induced episodic' and 'multi-trigger' wheeze perform poorly and should not be used.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Of children who wheeze as preschoolers, only half will still have asthma by school age.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A therapeutic trial of SABA or ICS may be needed to diagnose it**; ideally a health professional observes and documents the response to SABA.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No routine investigations: no chest X-ray; lung function tests cannot be used at this age.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **On ICS, measure height and weight at least annually, ideally every 3–6 months.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **MDI with spacer and facemask** until coordinated enough for the mouthpiece (often around 4 years).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Every child gets SABA with a spacer: salbutamol 100 mcg MDI, a maximum of 6 puffs**, spacer ± mask.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start a preventer for:** daytime symptoms at least 2 times weekly · night-time symptoms at least 2 times monthly · 2 or more hospital presentations in a year · 4 or more exacerbations a year.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First line: low-dose ICS — fluticasone propionate 50 mcg, 1 puff twice daily.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Montelukast is an alternative first line or an ICS add-on: 4 mg once daily (5 mg if over 5 years)** — useful when parents worry about steroids or MDI + spacer is very difficult.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **1 in 6 children on montelukast get agitation, sleep disturbance or mood change — stop it and see if they resolve.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Combination ICS/LABA is not recommended at this age** outside specialist use.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Review 8–12 weeks after starting.** If stable, trial off the preventer and reassess in 3 months; **stop it if the trial showed no benefit.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Control:** good = all of daytime symptoms and reliever use ≤2 days a week, no activity limitation, no night symptoms; partial = one or two failing; poor = three or more. Pre-exercise reliever doses don't count.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Review control in 6–12 weeks.** If poor, **check technique and adherence first**, consider other diagnoses, then step up.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **About 3 months of good control → consider stepping down.** Keep the lowest effective treatment; **cease only after 3 months symptom-free**, reviewing 4–6 weeks after each step down.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Not responding:** re-check the diagnosis, adherence and inhaler technique. **Refer** if control is inadequate at Step 4 or the diagnosis is uncertain.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Annual influenza vaccine; check adherence every visit; a written asthma action plan for home and childcare.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not increase the ICS dose during an exacerbation** in a child already on daily ICS.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not prescribe prednisolone for preschool asthma outside ED or hospital** — unless a GP is managing an exacerbation while arranging transfer to emergency.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Preschool asthma (1-5 years)' (Last updated June 2023), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Preschool_asthma_(1-5_years)/, retrieved 2026-09-23
